assessments.reasoning: Printed page 1.3 records the revision’s switch from deep to shallow binding. Page 12.1 describes the value cell, old value in the basic call frame and the restoration on function exit. Deutsch’s separate comparative paper explicitly attributes shallow binding to Interlisp-10.

challenge.method: Compare the enumerated alternatives and the LOCALVAR footnote with the earlier deep-binding edition and the revised Interlisp-D overview’s description of AltoLisp.
challenge.results: The four storage approaches visible in Section 12 have incompatible details. The October 1978 account selects the value-cell and basic-frame model. The original Interlisp-D overview reports deep binding for AltoLisp, so extending the claim to the entire implementation family would fail.

limitations: This is the documented Interlisp-10 mechanism for arguments actually bound through the described path. The test does not address nonlocal context transfers or local compiler declarations.
